ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The polygon enclosed by the solid lines in the figure consists of $ 4$ congruent squares joined edge-to-edge. One more congruent square is attached to an edge at one of the nine positions indicated. How many of the nine resulting polygons can be folded to form a cube with one face missing?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The gray solid-line part in the figure is composed of 4 congruent squares, and the shape is an L-shaped tetromino: there are 3 squares in the upper row, and there is also 1 square below the left-end square. The dashed lines give 9 addable positions: 7, 6, and 5 are respectively above the three gray squares in the upper row; 4 is to the right of the rightmost gray square; 3 is below the rightmost gray square; 2 is below the middle gray square; 1 is below the lower-left gray square; 8 is to the left of the upper-left gray square; 9 is to the left of the lower-left gray square. Reasoning: According to the method stated in the problem, label the gray L-shaped tetromino as A, B, C in the upper row from left to right, and D directly below A. Use the cube rolling rule to check each added position: let A occupy one face; each time moving along a common edge to an adjacent square is equivalent to rolling the cube 90 degrees; if the 5 squares fall on 5 different cube faces, then it can be folded into a cube missing one face. The basic 4 squares A, B, C, D can occupy 4 different faces. Check the added squares one by one: position 1 is below D, and after rolling it will fall on the same face as C, overlapping, so it cannot be used; position 3 is below C, and after rolling it will fall on the same face as D, so it cannot be used; position 2 is below B and adjacent to D, and will form a 2×2 cycle, producing inconsistency or overlapping faces when folded, so it cannot be used. Positions 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, and 9, after being added individually, all make the 5 squares occupy 5 different cube faces, so they can all be folded into a cube missing one face. There are 6 feasible positions in total.

raw_record.question_text: The polygon enclosed by the solid lines in the figure consists of 4 congruent squares joined edge-to-edge. One more congruent square is attached to an edge at one of the nine positions indicated. How many of the nine resulting polygons can be folded to form a cube with one face missing?

method.method_draft: Read the grey solid polygon as an L-shaped tetromino: three congruent squares in a horizontal row, with a fourth square directly below the leftmost one. Label these base squares A=(0,0), B=(1,0), C=(2,0), and D=(0,1). Read the dashed candidate attachment positions from the image as: 7 above A, 6 above B, 5 above C, 4 to the right of C, 3 below C, 2 below B, 1 below D, 8 left of A, and 9 left of D. For each candidate, test folding by the cube-rolling rule: assign A to one cube face, then when moving across a shared edge, roll the cube 90 degrees to determine which cube face the adjacent square would occupy. A resulting 5-square shape folds to a cube with one face missing exactly when the five squares occupy five distinct cube faces without forcing two squares onto the same face. Applying this: positions 1 and 3 force the added square onto a face already occupied by C or D respectively; position 2 creates a 2-by-2 cycle and also forces inconsistent/overlapping face assignments. Positions 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, and 9 give five distinct cube faces, so they work. Therefore the count is 6.

推理：按题设方法，把灰色L形四连方标为A、B、C在上排从左到右，D在A的正下方。用立方体滚动规则检查每个添加位置：令A占一个面，沿公共边每移动到相邻方格，就相当于把立方体滚动90度；若5个方格落在5个不同的立方体面上，则能折成缺一面的立方体。

基础4格A、B、C、D可占4个不同面。逐一检查添加格：位置1在D下方，滚动后会落到与C相同的面，重叠，不能用；位置3在C下方，滚动后会落到与D相同的面，不能用；位置2在B下方且与D相邻，会形成2×2循环，折叠时产生不一致或重叠面，不能用。位置4、5、6、7、8、9各自添加后都使5个方格占据5个不同的立方体面，因此都可以折成缺一面的立方体。

可行的位置共有6个。
